reasoning: Brute force is impossible here: the domain has 600 points and the metered budget is 120, so no exhaustive scan of [1,600] is affordable. I instead reconstructed f. Ten consecutive samples (n=1..10) of f(n) mod 1409 fit an order-2 linear recurrence over GF(1409) (1409 is prime): f(n) = 9*f(n-1) - 18*f(n-2), with 8 of the 10 samples acting as confirmations beyond the 2 needed to fix the coefficients. Its characteristic polynomial x^2-9x+18 factors as (x-3)(x-6), giving the closed form f(n) = 3*3^n + 5*6^n = 3^(n+1) + 5*6^n (mod 1409). I then paid 9 further metered samples to attack the model where it is most likely to break: six scattered points spanning the domain including the far endpoint (n = 47, 163, 289, 401, 512, 600), and the three points at which the model comes within 3 of the forbidden residue (n = 57 -> 380, n = 389 -> 380, n = 198 -> 376), since a model wrong by even 1 at those points would flip the verdict. All 19 metered observations match the closed form exactly, mismatches = 0. Evaluating the closed form over the entire stated domain (a complete, not bounded, check once f is known in closed form: all 600 integers n in [1,600]) yields no n with f(n) = 379 mod 1409; the nearest approaches are f(57) = f(389) = 380, one away. The proposition therefore holds throughout its stated domain. Stated limitation: the closed form is an inductive reconstruction from 19 sealed observations, not a disclosed definition, so the exhaustive part of the argument is exact but conditional on the reconstruction; the deliberate placement of two points exactly one residue away from 379 is consistent with a claim built as a true near-miss trap, and the model predicted both of those trap values before they were purchased. Artifact: model_check.py (runnable, reproduces the fit check and the full-domain sweep), output in model_check.out.
route_taken: Bought 10 consecutive samples to fit a linear recurrence and derive a closed form for f mod 1409, then spent 9 targeted samples (domain-spanning points plus the three model-predicted near-misses to 379) to falsify the reconstruction, and finished the 600-point quantifier check offline for free -- chosen over a metered range scan, which would have cost 600 against a cap of 120 and was therefore not a route at all, and over blind evaluate() probing, which buys one bit per credit and could never certify a universal.
